name: Denver Ventures
identity_check: Confirmed as Denver Ventures (denverventures.co), the Denver, Colorado early-stage investor at 1900 Lawrence Street, Suite 1930, formerly the Denver Angels angel group (co-founded 2016). Its legal page names the group as 'Denver Ventures, Denver Angels, DA Ventures'; BusinessDen (June 2025) describes Denver Ventures as the new parent of Denver Angels with a $20M seed fund; its LinkedIn page and database profiles (Fundable, IncubatorList) point to the same domain. The seed fund is filed with the SEC as DA Ventures Seed Fund I-A, LP and I-Q, LP (Denver, CO). This matches the lead (Pre-Seed to A, frontier/deep tech plus B2B software). Ruled out: Range Ventures and Access Venture Partners (other Denver-area VCs), a UK-listed 'DA VC / daventures vc' database entry (UK location, no link to denverventures.co), and the deal-by-deal SPV series filed as 'a Series of Denver Ventures I LLC' / 'Denver Angels LLC', which are this firm's syndicate vehicles, not separate investors.

open_items: Litigation: BusinessDen (2026-03-23) reports that Paul Foley, a Denver Angels co-founder and 20% owner, sued David Prichard, Kenneth Monfort and Zachary May on 2026-03-13 alleging theft, racketeering and securities fraud over the move of Denver Angels' value into Denver Ventures, plus malpractice against general counsel Jackson Killion. These are allegations; the defendants deny them. Outcome not checked.

No sector focus stated by the firm: the site says it is not limited by industry. The list's 'SaaS; Deep Tech' label is not on the site; the only deep-tech wording is a founder testimonial ('frontier technology investments in Colorado'). stated_sectors left out.

requires_us_entity and Indian founders: not stated. The site invests 'across the U.S.' with a Colorado emphasis; the HubSpot application form is rendered by script and its questions could not be read.

Fund documents: EDGAR full-text search lists Form D filings for DA Ventures Seed Fund I-A, LP and I-Q, LP (Delaware, Denver CO; filed 2023-04-19, amended 2024-04-10), but the SEC archive refused the declared User-Agent, so offering amount, amount sold and first-sale date were not read. Close date recorded is the June 2025 announcement date.

Syndicate vehicles: EDGAR shows dozens of deal-by-deal SPVs ('a Series of Denver Angels LLC' / 'a Series of Denver Ventures I LLC'), including 2025-2026 vehicles named for Aalo, Starfish Space, ElevenLabs, Ramp, Peak Energy, Tiny Health, Hydra, Boom Supersonic, RADICL and Agile. Not recorded as funds; amounts not read.

Portfolio companies with no round page naming the firm found: Kestrel Labs (database hint: Seed Fund I deal, March 2026), Meibel (database hint: April 2025), Hydra Host (its June 2026 $100M Series A release does not name Denver Ventures), Schematic ($6.5M post does not name it), Stridar, Steelhead Composites, Peak Energy, Starfish Space, Aalo, Boom Supersonic, Pepper, Tiny Health, Nymbl, CaliberMind 2025 Series B.

Urban Sky rounds (2023 Series A, 2025 Series B) name 'DA Ventures (a Denver Angels Affiliate)', i.e. the angel-group side before the Denver Ventures rebrand; the 2025 Series B article gives no day, so month precision. HQ country for Gravity and PostSig not stated on the round pages.

AUM: '$60 million in assets' combined for Denver Ventures and Denver Angels (BusinessDen, June 2025; VCJ 'over $60 million'); the lawsuit article cites $30M AUM for Denver Angels by 2023. The about page also claims '$15B Portfolio Capital Raised' and 650+ network investors. No schema field; noted only.
